title: Report: Aston Martin Delays EV Plans
summary: Aston Martin won’t build a pure electric vehicle until the company is forced to by legislation, says CEO Adrian Hallmark. body_markdown:
Aston Martin won’t build a pure electric vehicle until the company is forced to by legislation, says CEO Adrian Hallmark.


In an interview with *[Autocar](https://www.autocar.co.uk/car-news/new-cars/aston-wont-launch-ev-until-least-2033-will-keep-v8-and-v12)* , the former Bentley boss blamed customer demand and lawmakers for “changing way faster than any car company can cope with.”


“We only need BEVs to be compliant for legislative reasons just before 2035,” he said. “I’m not going to give an absolute date, because it’s imprecise. It could be 2035, it might be 2033, but it’s in that three-year window. It’s not 2031.”


Previously, Aston Martin stated that it would reveal its first EV before the end of 2025. That date got pushed to 2027, and now it could even be a full decade beyond that original promise.


In his former role, Hallmark would have witnessed the early development of Bentley’s first battery-electric vehicle, the[Torcal](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/torque-of-the-town-bentley-unveils-its-first-ev-the-torcal/) , but he is in no rush to repeat the exercise at Aston Martin, where the company will still produce V-8 and V-12 combustion cars for as long as possible. “We have a roadmap to keep the bigger and smaller engines alive and compliant all the way through to the end of that period,” he added.


In order to keep its ICE powertrains in production, Hallmark admitted that hybridization would likely be necessary, but “probably not plug-in, because we don’t need it; we don’t need the 200 kg (440 lb) penalties.”


When Aston Martin is eventually ready for electrification, the British company will lean on overseas expertise. Aston already has a deal in place with Lucid—which also gave the U.S. firm a 3.7 percent stake in Aston Martin—while long-term powertrain partner Mercedes-Benz could also supply EV propulsion.


“We have the deal with Lucid, and the interesting thing is, because we delayed, by the time we activate that deal, the technology that we will get is totally different to what we signed up the original contract for,” said Hallmark. “We’re also working with Mercedes-Benz on powertrains and electronic systems \[and that partnership\] will be deepened.”


Under Hallmark’s leadership, the traditional sounds, smells, and sensations of Aston Martins look to be safe. Now he just needs the loss-making brand to get back into the black.
